subject: CerebraHealth deployment acceptance criteria & procurement checklist
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@cerebrahealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference>
Cc: CerebraHealth Procurement <procurement@cerebrahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFI consolidation and deployment acceptance needs

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we start to finalize procurement and schedule the on-site install window, procurement needs a concise acceptance checklist and any evidence artifacts we can present to our auditors. Attached is a short list of questions/areas we need addressed by EOD Friday so the legal/procurement teams can finalize the SOW and PO:

- SP1: Does Redwood offer a fully air-gapped on-prem install (no outbound egress) and what are the installation pre-reqs?
- SP2: KMS integration options (customer KMS / HSM / local key storage) + key rotation cadence
- SP3: Evidence artifacts for SOC2 / control mapping + SBOM and cryptographic signing for patches
- SP4: Operator access model and any remote support options if environment is strictly sealed
- SP5: Acceptance tests: latency/load baseline, model output QA set, failover path and restoration window

Also please include any BOM or vendor-partner certification we need to include for our procurement route (we use CDW for hardware). I attached the consolidated RFI doc for reference.

Procurement timeline: target PO by 2028-03-08. If we cannot get these artifacts by then, procurement will push to the next cycle.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up if helpful.

Daniel
Director, Engineering Operations
CerebraHealth
procurement@cerebrahealth.com

Attachment: Cerebra_RFI_Capabilities_v3.docx

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@cerebrahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 01 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI consolidation and deployment acceptance needs

Daniel — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the timeline; attaching a compact acceptance matrix and the artifacts you asked for. Summary below (high level answers, see attachments for evidence):

- Air-gapped install: Yes — Redwood Private supports a fully offline on-prem installation. The on-prem package ships with an installer image and an operator-run offline patching flow. Installation pre-reqs: isolated management workstation for initial bootstrap, temporary outbound access allowed only for signature validation (can be replaced with air-signed artifacts provided to you).

- KMS options: Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM via VPN), on-prem HSM via PKCS#11, or local key store for strictly offline sites. Rotation cadence configurable; we recommend 90-day rotation for operator keys and annual rotation for root cipher material.

- SOC2 evidence + SBOM: Included in attachments: redwood_sbom_2028-02.zip and a control mapping excerpt. For patching we provide signed binaries; we can provide signature verification instructions for your security team. Full SOC2 report we can share under NDA with your security team (please confirm NDA contact).

- Operator access model: Role separation (Operator, Maintainer, Auditor). Operator accounts can be local-only; remote support is available via customer-approved jump host or via on-site engagement. We support operator credential rotation, per-session audit logging, and a read-only auditor role for telemetry access.

- Acceptance tests: We propose the following acceptance criteria (detailed in deployment_acceptance_matrix.xlsx):
  * Functional: model inference baseline trace for 100 sample prompts (golden-set) — deterministic regression < 2% on key metrics
  * Performance: 95th percentile latency under configured SLO for target request mix; throughput target validated with a 30-minute sustained load test
  * Resilience: simulated node and network failure with automatic failover to standby; full config restore tested within 48 hours (backup/restore playbook)

Attachments: deployment_acceptance_matrix.xlsx, redwood_sbom_2028-02.zip, network_topology_Cerebra.pdf

If it helps, we can provide a short operator-training engagement (3 days onsite) and an optional runbook handover during the acceptance window. We’ll also provide a CDW-compatible BOM for procurement.

I'll loop Laura and Marissa for operational and runbook details.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@cerebrahealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 01 Mar 2028 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI consolidation and deployment acceptance needs

Thanks Michael — this is great. Couple quick clarifying questions for the acceptance matrix so procurement can finalize language in the SOW:

1) Backup/restore: we list a 48-hour full-restore objective — is Cerebra comfortable with that window for the SOW? Some customers require 24 hours.
2) Failover: do you want explicit fallback to Redwood Hosted (cloud) models as a test step in the acceptance? For air-gapped customers that may not be allowable; we should offer an alternate verification method (local model variant fallback).
3) QA suite: please confirm the size of the golden prompt set (we propose 100 prompts) and whether you require any domain-specific prompts from Cerebra for the regression check.

Daniel — if you can confirm 1–3 we’ll bake the accepted language into the SOW and the DocuSign draft.

Laura
Senior Product Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@cerebrahealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 01 Mar 2028 13:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFI consolidation and deployment acceptance needs

Looping in a couple operational details from the runbook that typically go into the SOW/acceptance annex. See runbook snippet in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRunbookLink

- Operator rotation: default policy is 90-day rotation for operator credentials; emergency rotation playbook included.
- Patch verification for air-gapped sites: signed patches are shipped as artifacts and verified via offline signature tool. We can provide either the signing public key or host a signature verification appliance on your network.
- Rollback: we recommend a staged rollback plan (config snapshot + application-level checkpoint). For SOW we usually accept a 48-hour full-restoration SLA; if you need 24-hour restore we’ll need to schedule additional engineering validation during the acceptance window.

Attachment: operator-training-outline.pdf

Thanks everyone for the fast turnaround. A few clarifications from procurement/security:

- Backup/restore: procurement prefers 24-hour full restore in the SOW. If Redwood cannot commit to 24 hours we will accept 48 hours but need explicit language about the mitigation steps and any escalation credits.
- SOC2 evidence: procurement will accept a redacted SOC2 report under NDA. I’ll send an NDA to your security inbox (security@cerebrahealth.com). Can you confirm timeline for that?
- CDW BOM: please send a CDW-certified bill of materials (line items and part numbers) so procurement can route the hardware purchase via their existing contract.

Next steps: procurement will prepare the PO template if we get final SOW and BOM by 2028-03-06. Please include a DocuSign-ready SOW PDF.

Attaching acceptance ticket: Cerebra_Acceptance_Ticket_12345.pdf

Daniel — appreciate the prompt. Confirming deliverables and schedule:

- We will accept a 48-hour full restore in the SOW by default. If Cerebra requires 24-hour restore, we can add a validation sprint to the SOW (two engineer-days) and capture the SLA in the commercial appendix (we'll provide escalation credit language).
- SOC2: we can provide a redacted SOC2 report. Security team will reach out to the NDA contact today. Timeline: redacted report available within 2 business days after NDA confirmation.
- CDW BOM: attached a CDW-friendly BOM and the final SOW draft for DocuSign. Please review and let us know edits tonight; we’ll push the DocuSign envelope first thing tomorrow.

Attachments: final_sow_Cerebra_20280302.pdf
DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/ABC-SOW-Cerebra-20280302

Next steps (summary):
1) Cerebra confirms restore window (24h vs 48h) — reply to this thread by EOD.
2) Procurement confirms PO path and provides hardware lead times.
3) Security completes NDA so we can send the SOC2 artifact.
4) We schedule a 60-minute pre-install kickoff after PO execution to finalize access and install dates.

If you want an engineer on the call tomorrow to talk through the operator handoff and signature verification for offline patches, we can make time.

—Michael
